THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Deli Dill Snack Box

Snack Box Series Ep. 8 — deli-plate energy at snack-box scale. 2.5 oz deli turkey + cubed Colby Jack + petite dill pickles + pretzel crisps. About 250 cal / 20g protein per box. Ep. 8 returns to shelf-stable proteins after Ep. 7's first-hot-protein Tropical Chicken. Make four at once for 2 kids × 2 days.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME10 min active — no cook, assembly only
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~250 cal | ~20g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: PRETZELS GO IN THE DRY COMPARTMENT — separated from pickle moisture. Pretzel + pickle contact = soft mush within hours. This is Ep. 8's most texture-critical rule.

Ingredients

PER BOX (yields 1 snack box)

  • 2.5 oz deli turkey (or 3 oz for hungrier kids)
  • 1 Colby Jack cheese stick, cubed
  • 3-4 petite dill pickles
  • 0.75 oz pretzel crisps

FOUR-BOX BATCH (recommended)

  • 10 oz deli turkey (or 12 oz for the hungrier version)
  • 4 Colby Jack cheese sticks
  • 12-16 petite dill pickles
  • 3 oz pretzel crisps

Allergens: dairy, gluten, wheat.

You want the classic deli-plate flavor profile (turkey + cheese + pickles + pretzels) in a make-four-at-once snack box that lasts 2 kids × 2 days. Ep. 8 of the Split Plate Snack Box series — returns to shelf-stable proteins (deli turkey) after Ep. 7's cooked-fajita-chicken exception. Wider cold-chain tolerance than Ep. 7 (deli turkey holds better than cooked chicken). Assembles like a lunchable but eats like a real deli plate.

Method

  1. 1.SET UP. Set out four divided snack boxes (4-compartment Bento-style — same format as Snack Box Series Ep. 1-7). Deli turkey is shelf-stable pre-open; no cooking needed. Ep. 8 returns to shelf-stable proteins after Ep. 7's cooked-fajita-chicken exception.
  2. 2.TURKEY. Divide 10 oz deli turkey into 4 boxes — 2.5 oz per box. Any oven-roasted deli turkey works (Hillshire Farm Premium Carved shown; brand-neutral by default). For hungrier kids or adult mini-meal, bump to 3 oz per box (12 oz total).
  3. 3.COLBY JACK. Cube one Colby Jack cheese stick per box and add to the second compartment. Cube size = 1/2-inch or smaller for young kids. Colby Jack is milder than sharp cheddar — kid-friendly by default. Uniform cube size = no compartment ends up with awkward pieces.
  4. 4.PICKLES. Add 3-4 petite dill pickles per box to the third compartment (Mt. Olive Kosher Dill Petites shown). This is the flavor-identity moment — kids either love it or reject it, which is the caption's engagement hook. For under-4s, slice petites lengthwise to reduce choking risk; over 4s handle whole petites fine with supervision.
  5. 5.PRETZELS. Add 0.75 oz pretzel crisps (Snack Factory Original shown) to the DRY compartment — critical to keep pretzels away from pickle moisture, else they soften in the sealed box within hours. Pretzel crisps are flat and thin so they hold better than round hard pretzels, but still separate compartments.
  6. 6.LID + CHILL. Snap lids on and refrigerate immediately. Assembled boxes hold up to 3 days for the turkey + cheese (deli turkey has wider cold-chain tolerance than Ep. 7's cooked chicken). Pretzels stay crunchy for 2-3 days if separated from pickle moisture in the box. For lunchboxes, pack with an ice pack.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid: Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • Cube Colby Jack uniformly — 1/2-inch or smaller for young kids. Uniform cube size = no compartment ends up with awkwardly-sized pieces.
  • Slice petite pickles lengthwise for kids under 4 (whole petites are choking-appropriate for over-4s with supervision). Per CDC + AAP choking-prevention guidance.

If something fails

Pretzels went soft in the box: Pickle moisture migrated to the pretzel compartment. Use a divided box with tall walls between compartments, or add pretzels closer to serving (in a separate mini-container) instead of at assembly. Pretzel crisps hold better than round hard pretzels but still soften from trapped humidity.

Pickles leaked juice into the turkey compartment: Overpacked or pickles too wet. Pat pickles with a paper towel before placing, or use fewer petites per box. Divided boxes with tall walls help — some Bento-style boxes have flat wells that don't contain liquid well.

Kid won't touch the pickles: This is Ep. 8's engagement hook — some kids love dill, some reject it hard. Swap for cucumber slices (mild flavor, similar visual role), diced red bell pepper (sweet-savory), or halved cherry tomatoes for the compartment. The third compartment is a flex slot.

Colby Jack is too mild for adults stealing a box: Sub sharp cheddar or pepper jack for the adult portion. Cube smaller for adult variety too — small cubes read snackier than a full stick.

Turkey feels dry after 2 days in the fridge: Deli turkey loses moisture in a sealed compartment. Add a small squeeze of lemon or a drizzle of olive oil at serve time, or use it within day 1-2 for best texture. Never repack turkey that's been at room temp for more than 2 hours.

Box smells like pickle brine after 1 day: Pickle moisture is escaping the compartment. Try patting pickles dry before placing, or use a box with tighter compartment seals. The brine smell doesn't ruin the food but reads unappealing at snack time.

Storage and reheating

Store: Assemble the 4 boxes in one 10-minute pass. Refrigerate immediately. Assembled boxes hold up to 3 days — longest of the snack box series thanks to shelf-stable deli turkey (Ep. 7 caps at 2 days because of cooked chicken). Pretzels stay crunchy for 2-3 days if kept in the dry compartment. For lunchboxes, pack with an ice pack.

Reheat: Don't reheat the assembled box (cheese sweats, pickles taste off warm). Serve chilled by default — that's the whole snack-box format. For adult mini-meal use, warm the turkey portion briefly if desired, but repack after cooling.

Lasts: 3 days max in the fridge — the pretzel crunch is the first thing to degrade after that, followed by pickle-to-pretzel moisture migration. Deli turkey shelf life is 3-5 days from opening but the assembled box caps at 3 for pretzel texture. Adding pretzels closer to serving extends the crunch window.

Estimated nutrition

~250 cal | ~20g protein.

About 250 cal / 20g protein per snack box — user-approved headline, not label-verified. Broad component approximation: 2.5 oz deli turkey (~75 cal / 15g protein) + 1 Colby Jack stick (~80 cal / 5g protein) + 3-4 petite dill pickles (~5-10 cal / ~0g protein) + 0.75 oz pretzel crisps (~90 cal / 2g protein) ≈ 250 cal / 22g protein. Rounds to the user-approved ~250 / 20 published headline as a practical allowance for brand + portion variation. Verify against your exact labels before publishing as macro-accurate. Deli turkey is the protein anchor; upgrade to 3 oz per box pushes to ~275 cal / 24g protein. Not sponsored, not endorsed, not affiliated with Hillshire Farm, Sargento, Mt. Olive, Snack Factory, or any specific deli turkey / cheese stick / pickle / pretzel brand.

Adult plate | Kid plate

Adult plate

Adult

Adult-friendly batch too — steal a box from the meal-prep stack. ~250 cal / 20g protein reads as a clean parent snack. Deli turkey is the shelf-stable protein anchor, easier to pack than Ep. 7's cooked chicken. Adults can bump turkey to 3 oz per box (~275 cal / 24g protein) if snack-as-mini-meal.

Kid plate

Kid

SAFETY: Whole petite pickles + firm cheese cubes are texture-appropriate for most kids but under 4s should have pickles sliced lengthwise (not left whole) and cheese cubed small (1/2-inch or less). Pretzel crisps are flat and thin — lower choking risk than round hard pretzels, but still watch for kids who don't chew thoroughly. Per CDC + AAP choking-prevention guidance. Kids can help place components — turns snack prep into low-pressure participation. Not school-safe by default: some schools restrict pretzel wheat/gluten; check the school's allergen and formulation rules before packing outside the home.

Three keys to success

  1. 1PRETZELS GO IN THE DRY COMPARTMENT — separated from pickle moisture. Pretzel + pickle contact = soft mush within hours. This is Ep. 8's most texture-critical rule.
  2. 2Cube Colby Jack uniformly — 1/2-inch or smaller for young kids. Uniform cube size = no compartment ends up with awkwardly-sized pieces.
  3. 3Slice petite pickles lengthwise for kids under 4 (whole petites are choking-appropriate for over-4s with supervision). Per CDC + AAP choking-prevention guidance.

Brands I use

Hillshire Farm Premium Carved (any oven-roasted deli turkey)
2.5 oz per box (10 oz total). Hillshire Farm Premium Carved Oven Roasted Turkey Breast shown; brand-neutral by default.
Shelf-stable protein anchor. Deli turkey has wider cold-chain tolerance than Ep. 7's cooked fajita chicken — easier to pack for lunchboxes. Any oven-roasted deli turkey works; label carries the exact macro count. Not sponsored, not endorsed, not affiliated.
Colby Jack cheese sticks (any brand)
1 stick per box, cubed. Sargento, Frigo, Kirkland all flex.
Creamy calcium + mild kid-friendly flavor. Milder than sharp cheddar. Cube uniformly (1/2-inch or smaller for young kids). Any brand works; the label carries the exact calorie/protein count that anchors the macro estimate.
Mt. Olive Kosher Dill Petites (or any brand of petite dills)
3-4 petite pickles per box. Petite pickles are whole small pickles vs sliced dills.
The flavor-identity moment for Ep. 8 — deli-plate energy comes from the dill briny note. Petites are choking-appropriate for over-4s with supervision; slice lengthwise for under-4s. Any brand works; kosher dill petites hold their crunch better than pickle chips. Not sponsored.
Snack Factory Original Pretzel Crisps (or any pretzel-crisp brand)
0.75 oz per box. Flat/thin pretzels hold crunch better in a sealed box than round hard pretzels.
The dry-compartment crunch. Pretzel crisps' flat shape holds crunch better vs round hard pretzels in a sealed humid box. Any pretzel-crisp brand flexes; standard round pretzels are a fallback but soften faster. Contains wheat/gluten — not school-safe if the school restricts gluten. Not sponsored.
